video_goal: Demonstrate how to adjust the height and depth of the lumbar support pad on a Herman Miller Aeron chair.
required_subjects_and_props: Herman Miller Aeron chair, removable lumbar support pad, person (hands and body)

outline_steps.visual_action: A person stands behind an empty Herman Miller Aeron chair, highlighting the dark, woven pellicle mesh back.
The camera focuses on the horizontal lumbar support pad resting on the vertical tracks directly behind the mesh.
The person's hands reach out and firmly grasp both outer edges of the lumbar support pad.
The hands slide the lumbar pad smoothly upward along the vertical tracks to the highest position.
The hands slide the lumbar pad downward to the lowest position on the tracks.
The fingers grip the textured rubber edge of the pad, preparing to remove it for depth adjustment.
The hands pull the lumbar pad firmly backward, snapping it completely off the vertical tracks.
The hands rotate the removed lumbar pad 180 degrees to reveal the thicker, more pronounced side of the pad.
The hands align the grooves on the thicker side of the pad with the vertical tracks on the chair frame.
The hands push forward, snapping the lumbar pad securely back onto the tracks.
The person walks around to the front of the Herman Miller Aeron chair and sits down on the seat pan.
The person leans back into the pellicle mesh, pressing their lower back against the newly adjusted lumbar pad.
